short: Five centuries of Mediterranean dominion, from Augustus to the deposition of Romulus Augustulus.
full:
The Roman Empire is conventionally dated from 27 BCE, when the Senate granted Octavian the title Augustus and the Republic became a monarchy in all but name. At its greatest extent under Trajan it stretched from northern Britain to Mesopotamia, governing perhaps a fifth of the world's population.

Its durability rested on engineering, law and citizenship: roads and aqueducts that outlasted the state itself, a legal tradition that underpins most European codes today, and a willingness to extend Roman citizenship to conquered peoples. The Western Empire fragmented under fiscal strain, civil war and migration, ending in 476 CE when Odoacer deposed Romulus Augustulus. The Eastern, Byzantine, half endured until 1453.
